segments.text: Listening Test In the listening test, you will be asked
to demonstrate how well you understand spoken English.
The entire listening test will last approximately 45 minutes.
There are four parts and directions are given for each part.
You must mark your answers on the separate answer sheet.
Do not write your answers in your test book.
Part 1.
Directions For each question in this part, you will
hear four statements about a picture in your test book.
When you hear the statements, you must select the one statement that best describes what
you see in the picture.
Then find the number of the question on your answer sheet and mark your answer.
The statements will not be printed in your test book and will be spoken only one time.
Now part 1 will begin.
Number 1.
Look at the picture marked number 1 in your test book.
A, a man is reading a book, B, a man is sitting at a table, C, a man is opening a window,
D, a man is pushing a cart.
Number 2.
Look at the picture marked number 2 in your test book.
A, some benches have been placed under a pavilion, B, some plants are arranged around
a lamppost, C, there's a fountain beside the pathway, D, some trees are shading the
benches.
Number 3.
Look at the picture marked number 3 in your test book.
A, they're going into a building, B, they're loading some luggage, C, they're taking off
their jackets, D, they're walking outside.
Number 4.
Look at the picture marked number 4 in your test book.
A, a server is watering some plants, B, some people are seated at the tables, C, a server
is stacking some chairs, D, umbrellas have been opened over the tables.
Number 5.
Look at the picture marked number 5 in your test book.
A, she has opened a refrigerator, B, she is carrying a basket, C, she is pushing a cart
along an aisle, D, she has stacked boxes on a shelf.
Number 6.
Look at the picture marked number 6 in your test book.
A, he's kneeling on the floor, B, he's reaching for a sign,
C, he's carrying a basket, D, he's talking on a phone.
Part 2.
Directions
You will hear a question or statement and three responses spoken in English.
They will not be printed in your test book and will be spoken only one time.
Select the best response to the question or statement and mark the letter A, B or C on
your answer sheet.
Now, let us begin with question number 7.
Number 7.
Who's going to report on the City Council election next week?
A, the council meets on Thursday evening, B, she filed her report on time, C, one of
the newer staff writers I believe.
Number 8.
Which counter should I take my golf clubs to for check in?
A, any of the oversized baggage desks will handle those.
B, I checked in online this morning.
C, the departure gate is on the upper level.
Number 9.
Where's the lead architect working these days?
A, a brand new hospital project.
B, she's our best architect, definitely.
C,
Oh, the design team shifted up to the third floor.
Number 10.
Are you running the children's story hour this afternoon?
A, Lauren is covering it for me.
B, the store closes at 6.
C, that works for me.
Number 11.
How did the sign-ups for our new swimming lessons turn out this season?
A, the swelling lessons after a day or two.
B, she teaches the morning swim class.
C, they came in nearly a third higher than last year.
Number 12.
Why did Nathan get to the studio so late this morning?
A, the morning traffic report.
B, in the second studio.
C, because his bus broke down.
Number 13.
There's a spot open on the lighting crew for the next show.
A, no, the lights are all turned off now.
B, actually I've done that kind of work before.
C, they said the rehearsal ran a bit late.
Number 14.
When does the evening spin class begin?
A, not for another 20 minutes.
B,
Yes, she's just a beginner.
C, in the studio downstairs.
Number 15.
Where's this year's charity Gala being held?
A, it's over at the Grand View Ballroom.
B, we're still a bit short on volunteers.
C, at 7 o'clock I think.
Number 16.
Please stock the refrigerator with fresh ingredients before the evening service starts.
A,
Right behind the prep counter near the sink.
B,
I'll take care of that as soon as I finish this order.
C, no, the soup came out a little cold.
Number 17.
Has our building permit been issued yet?
A, right around the corner.
B,
The inspector still has to sign off.
C,
My magazine issue arrived today.
Number 18.
Is the greenhouse tour led by a guide or are we free to walk through it on our own?
A,
The guide should be here soon.
B,
Past the flower beds.
C,
You're welcome to go through it yourselves.
Number 19.
Would you rather run the new campaign on the radio or online?
A,
Could you turn the radio down?
B,
Most of our customers are teenagers.
The election results came out yesterday.
Number 20.
Could you recommend somewhere nearby to grab lunch?
A,
The recommendation letter is on your desk.
B,
I usually bring my own lunch.
C,
There's a great sandwich place just around the corner.
Number 21.
When will my prescription be ready?
A,
At the pharmacy on the corner.
B,
Once this afternoon's delivery arrives.
C,
Just two boxes left in stock.
Number 22.
How did the weekend charity run turn out?
A,
You can register at the front desk.
B,
Turn right at the second light.
C,
I was out of town all weekend.
Number 23.
When are we supposed to hear back from the property inspector?
A,
Not until Thursday most likely.
B,
Down in the basement I think.
C,
Sure, that works for me.
Number 24.
How are we going to cut down on all this wasted fabric?
A,
By laying the pieces closer together.
B,
She usually works in the cutting room.
C,
No,
It wasn't a waste of money.
Number 25.
Isn't Warren the one who fitted my new glasses?
A,
Right over by the window display.
B,
Yes, he's helping someone right now.
C,
No,
The classes begin at nine.
Number 26.
Once you're planning to take the photography class this evening.
A,
A very talented photographer.
B,
They cancelled it this morning.
C,
I'll get it done soon.
Number 27.
Do you know if this novel is available in paperback?
A,
They're right at the back of the store.
B,
Yes, I lent her my copy last week.
C,
I'll look it up in our system.
Number 28.
Why didn't Wesley take the early route into the city this morning?
A,
Not until nearly nine.
B,
His van broke down.
C,
Right past the city center.
Number 29.
You've already backed up the server files, haven't you?
A,
The system's been down all morning.
B,
No,
The printouts haven't been collected.
C,
About 20 gigabytes total.
Number 30.
Why did you close your register so early tonight?
A,
Because there weren't any shoppers left.
B,
Just past the produce section.
C,
We close at 10 on weekends.
Number 31.
When does the next ferry to the island leave?
A,
From Pier 5,
B,
The island's really lovely this time of year.
C,
In about 20 minutes.
Part 3.
Directions.
You will hear some conversations between two or more people.
You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say in each conversation.
Select the best response to each question and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet.
The conversations will not be printed in your testbook and will be spoken only one time.
Questions 32-34 refer to the following conversation.
Morning Colin,
I wanted to let you know that our annual inventory count is happening this Thursday
and will count the small items in the back stock room.
Because of it, the store will close early to customers at 6 instead of the usual 9.
Oh, I didn't realize it was already that time of year.
Does that mean my evening shift on the sales floor is cancelled?
No, not at all.
I'd actually like you to help the team count the merchandise once the doors close.
Plan on staying until about 10, since it usually takes a few hours.
Number 32.
Where will some items be counted according to the woman?
Number 33.
What role does the man most likely have?
Number 34.
Why is the man expected to stay late?
Questions 35-37 refer to the following conversation.
Hello, I'm calling about a flight that just landed a little while ago.
Silverwing Airlines Flight 512.
I believe I left my reading glasses in a small case in the seat pocket
and I'm really hoping to get them back.
I can certainly help with that.
Can you tell me which seat you were sitting in?
The thing is, when a flight arrives, lost items aren't brought up to our office right away.
The cleaning crew has to go through the whole cabin first, so it hasn't reached us yet.
Oh, I see.
The trouble is, I have a connecting flight in about an hour, so I'm a little worried about waiting that long.
I completely understand.
Let me call one of my colleagues down at the gate and see if she can find the case for you sooner.
Give me just a moment.
Number 35.
What is the main reason for the woman's call?
Number 36.
What issue does the man explain?
Number 37.
What action will the man take next?
Questions 38-40 refer to the following conversation.
Good afternoon.
Thanks for calling Marsden Lock and Key.
This is Leon speaking.
How can I help you today?
Hi.
I just bought an older house on Harwick Road, and although the back door is fine, the front door lock is really worn out.
I'd like to have a completely new one installed.
Sure.
I can set that up for you.
Before I check the schedule, is it just the front door, or do you need any other doors done as well?
Just the front door for now.
The key sticks every time I try to turn it.
So how soon could someone come out?
Good news there.
We have a technician free this afternoon after a job nearby, so we can take care of it the same day.
Oh, that's wonderful.
The house number is 14 Harwick Road.
Do I pay now, or do you send something first?
No payment is needed yet.
I'll send you a confirmation message with the time and the technician's name.
Number 38.
Why is the woman calling?
Number 39.
What does the man mention about the service?
Number 40.
What does the man say he will do next?
Questions 41 through 43 refer to the following conversation.
Hi.
I'm calling the set up my daughter's birthday party next Saturday.
Do you have any open lanes that afternoon, maybe after lunch?
We do have space then.
I just checked our party package list, and shoe rental for everyone in your group is included in the price.
Great.
That helps.
We'll have about 12 bowlers, plus a few parents watching, so I think we'll need three lanes around two o'clock.
Three lanes at two will work.
I can hold them until tonight, but to secure the reservation, please pay a small deposit through our website.
Number 41.
Where does the woman most likely work?
Number 42.
What has the woman just done?
Number 43.
What is the man expected to do next?
Questions 44 through 46 refer to the following conversation.
Good afternoon, Ashgrove Community Sports League.
This is Marcus.
How can I help you today?
Hi.
My name is Colleen Farrell, and I'm calling about joining one of your recreational volleyball teams.
Sure, Colleen.
Have you played in our league before, or are you new to Ashgrove?
I moved to Ashgrove last month, so I haven't signed up before, but I'm hoping to meet people outside work.
Welcome to the neighborhood.
Let me pull up the roster for the Tuesday evening division.
The current session's teams are already full, although a new beginner-friendly session is forming soon.
That sounds promising.
When does that new session start, and is there anything I should do before then?
It begins early next month at the community center.
To reserve your spot, you'll need to register through our website by Friday.
I can email you the link to the form after this call.
Number 44.
Why is the woman calling?
Number 45.
What does the woman say she recently did?
Number 46.
What does the man say the woman needs to do?
Questions 47-49 refer to the following conversation.
Okay, so we need to wrap up the user manual for the new app by Friday.
I've already drafted the whole first chapter, the getting started walkthrough.
Nice work.
But I'm a little worried.
There are quite a few advanced features to document, and Friday isn't far off.
Can we really cover everything in time?
I think so, if we divide it up.
Why don't you take the configuration section and all handle the troubleshooting chapter?
The only catch is, both parts rely on the updated interface screenshots being in place before we finalize.
Right.
And those are still sitting with the design team.
So I'll have to run it by them before we can drop anything in.
Let me reach out to them now, thanks.
While you do that, I'll keep polishing from the draft we already have.
Actually, one more issue.
The draft is close to our shared drives 50 megabyte per file cap.
Since you'll be working from it, we should probably confirm it can even be pushed up before we get too far.
Number 47.
What are the speakers discussing?
Number 48.
What will the woman check with the design team about?
Number 49.
What will the man most likely do next?
Questions 50 through 52 refer to the following conversation.
Hi, I'm putting together the costumes for a stage play our community theater is running next month.
And I need about a dozen period costumes.
Is that something your shop can help with?
Absolutely.
We carry a full range of historical costumes.
I'd recommend reserving them as soon as you can though.
This time of year, our inventory tends to book up very quickly.
Good to know.
Could you check whether you have 12 available in the right sizes?
I'll email you all the cast measurements later today so you have the exact numbers.
Number 50.
According to the man, what is planned for next month?
Number 51.
Where does the woman probably work?
Number 52.
Which task does the man offer to complete?
Questions 53 through 55 refer to the following conversation.
Deborah, I just finished counting the register totals and I've got some good news.
Those handmade pottery pieces we started carrying last week are already sold out.
That's wonderful.
We've been trying for months to give the local artists more space here.
So this really proves the idea works.
Exactly.
I think people coming out of the new exhibit want to take home something special.
And the price is low enough that almost everyone buys one.
We went through all 40 pieces in just three days.
The shelf by the counter is already completely full though.
That's a fair point.
What if we set up a separate display table near the museum entrance just for the pottery?
That way we could stock a lot more and let visitors see it the moment they walk in.
Number 53.
Where most likely are the speakers?
Number 54.
Why does the woman say the shelf by the counter is already completely full?
Number 55.
What does the man suggest doing to sell more pottery?
Questions 56 through 58 refer to the following conversation.
Hi, my name's Bruno.
I'm calling because my band would like to reserve a room at Tidewater Sound next month.
Do you have any openings?
Thanks for calling Bruno.
We have several weekdays available but weekend sessions are nearly full.
How much time do you think you'll need?
A full day should be enough if that's possible.
We have five songs ready and we'd rather record them all together.
That should work. I'd also recommend adding our mixing service.
Our engineer can balance the tracks afterward so the finished songs sound clear and ready to share.
That's good to know.
We've never released anything professionally before.
In that case, I'd suggest it.
I'll email you our full price list first.
If those costs work for you, I can then hold the room and ask the engineer to join the session.
Number 56.
What type of business is the man contacting?
Number 57.
What is the point of the man's comment?
We've never released anything professionally before.
Number 58.
What is the woman's next planned action?
Questions 59-61 refer to the following conversation.
I was checking the lunch file because the menu estimate looked high and I found a message from Rosewood catering.
They are completely booked and can't handle the staff appreciation lunch on Friday.
Oh no, that's only two weeks away and the dining room is already reserved.
I know.
Well, we could move the lunch to Thursday afternoon when Rosewood still has staff free.
Or ask the office team to choose a simpler menu.
Hmm, I'd rather not change the date or the plan.
Everyone's already put Friday on their calendars and the simpler menu wouldn't feel much like an appreciation lunch.
There's a new company that just opened downtown, Copper Spoon catering.
We could try them instead.
We've never used them before.
Uh, where did you hear about them?
A few people from the design firm next door recommended them.
I'll set up a food tasting this week so we can see exactly what they offer.
If the food isn't right, we'll keep Rosewood's Thursday opening as a backup.
Number 59.
What problem does the woman identify?
Number 60.
Why does the woman say we've never used them before?
Number 61.
What does the man say he will do?
Question 62 through 64 refer to the following conversation and diagram.
Hi, I'd like to order the Sun Ridge play set for my garden.
And I'm also hoping to schedule the installation crew for next weekend.
There's a strict two and a half meter height limit for any structure in my yard.
We can pencil in a Saturday installation once your order is confirmed.
The Sun Ridge has four sections at different heights,
and customers often adjust which pieces they include.
Take a look at this diagram.
Thanks.
A few of these look like they could push the limit.
Is there any flexibility for a section that's close?
First thing tomorrow, I'll get in touch with the manufacturer and ask whether the swing beam can be trimmed.
But one of the sections is a fixed frame and can't be modified at all.
Actually, the swing beam still measures under my limit as it stands, so that one's fine.
But one section clearly goes over the two and a half meters.
Let's leave that section out of the order.
Number 62.
What are the speakers mainly discussing?
Number 63.
What does the man say he will do tomorrow?
Number 64.
Look at the graphic.
Which section will be left out of the order?
Question 65 through 67 refer to the following conversation and chart.
I'm glad you could stop by, Glenn.
I'm a bit worried about the parking situation.
The lot fills up before 9 every morning and I really think we need to get more of those commuters onto our buses instead.
I understand the concern, Nora, but the numbers are actually encouraging.
If you look at this chart, the route we added just last year is already carrying 24% of our riders, so the demand is clearly there.
That's great news.
I'd like to put a few extra buses on that route during the morning rush.
I've already got the trip schedule pulled up here, but can you check the driver roster?
I want to make sure we have enough people to cover the additional trips.
Sure.
Let me run down to the front desk and grab it right now.
Number 65.
What are the speakers mainly discussing?
Number 66.
Look at the graphic.
Which route does the man mention?
Number 67.
What will the man go get?
Question 68 through 70 refer to the following conversation and table.
Hi.
I'd like to have a document translated, please.
It's a personal certificate.
Just a single page, but I need it to be an official translation.
Of course, we can do that for you.
We offer several turnaround options, and each one has a different price.
If you take a look at the rate table posted on the wall behind you, you can see how many
days each level takes.
Thanks.
The thing is, I'm on a bit of a deadline.
I have to submit this certificate by the end of the week.
I need the finished translation back within two days at the latest.
And out of whichever levels meet that, I'd like the least expensive one.
Got it.
That works fine.
I'll set that up for you right now, and once it's processed, I'll send you a confirmation
by email with all the details.
Number 68.
What does the woman say she wants translated?
Number 69.
Look at the graphic.
Which service will the woman most likely choose?
Number 70.
What does the man offer to do?
Part 4.
Directions.
You will hear some talks given by a single speaker.
You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speaker says in each talk.
Select the best response to each question and mark the letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet.
The talks will not be printed in your testbook and will be spoken only one time.
Question 71 through 73.
Refer to the following announcement.
Attention everyone, and thank you for spending the day with us.
We will be closing in 20 minutes so we kindly ask all visitors to begin making their way
toward the main exit near the front gate.
Please note that our gift shop by the entrance will remain open for an additional half hour
in case you'd like to pick up a souvenir before you leave.
Here at Willowmere Wildlife Park, we're also preparing for a busy weekend.
This Saturday, we'll be holding a special evening event with lantern lit trails and a chance to see some of our nocturnal animals after dark.
Spaces are limited, so if you're interested in joining us, please stop by the information desk on your way out to reserve your tickets.
We hope you've enjoyed your visit and we look forward to seeing you again soon.
Number 71.
Where are listeners hearing this announcement?
Number 72.
What are visitors asked to start doing?
Number 73.
What does the announcer say is scheduled for this Saturday?
Question 74 through 76 refer to the following tour information.
Good morning everyone and welcome to Hollowbrook Coffee Roastery.
Before we set off, please pick up a headset from the front counter.
The machines get quite loud so you'll need one to hear me clearly.
Here's how our visit will go.
We'll start in the roasting hall because a fresh batch is being roasted right now and I want you to see the whole process.
After that, we'll move to the sorting room, then the tasting room and we'll finish in the packing area.
Now, a lot of visitors ask me about our different blends.
Personally, I always reach for our morning amber blend.
Number 74.
What does the speaker tell the listeners to pick up at the front counter?
Number 75.
Why will the tour begin in the roasting hall?
Number 76.
Why does the speaker say, personally, I always reach for our morning amber blend?
Questions 77 through 79 refer to the following advertisement.
Are you planning a spring move while Lakeside Radio's morning home is on, but dreading all the boxes in heavy furniture?
Well, there's no need to worry because the team at Ocave and Movers is here to make your move simple and stress-free.
From the first room you pack to the final doorway at your new place.
For more than 15 years, we've helped families and small offices across the region move quickly and safely.
And our trained crew handles everything from careful packing to loading, transport and unloading.
Right now, we're offering a special spring deal.
Book your move before the end of March and you'll receive 20% off the total price.
Just call us today at 555 0182 to check open dates and let us do the heavy lifting.
Number 77.
What is being advertised?
Number 78.
What must listeners do to qualify for the discount?
Number 79.
What does the speaker mean when she says, let us do the heavy lifting?
Questions 80 through 82 refer to the following broadcast.
Good afternoon and welcome to the Arts Hour here on Bayside Community Radio.
Our top story today, a striking new mural has just been unveiled on the west wall of the downtown parking garage.
It's the work of more than 20 local artists who spent the past three months painting it together
and it's now the largest outdoor artwork anywhere in our region.
To mark the occasion, the city is hosting a free celebration this Saturday afternoon
with music and food right beside the mural.
Because seating at the event is limited, we strongly recommend that you reserve a spot online
through the city's website in advance.
And now, stay with us because right after this, we'll be talking live with Harold Quinn,
the lead artist behind the project.
Number 80.
What kind of event is planned for Saturday afternoon?
Number 81.
What action are people urged to take?
Number 82.
What is scheduled to come immediately after this segment?
Questions 83 through 85 refer to the following broadcast.
In local news, snack food maker Bright Vale Foods has confirmed it will move its headquarters
to Harlingen early next spring.
The company, which produces packaged baked goods for supermarkets,
expects to relocate about 400 employees to the area.
Local hotels and restaurants are especially pleased as managers anticipate a steady stream
of visiting staff, sales representatives and out of town clients.
The mayor said the decision also puts Harlingen on the map for other consumer goods firms.
Traffic on the town's main roads is expected to grow heavier,
and the company has promised to fund improvements at two busy intersections.
Yes, the extra congestion will be a nuisance,
but the jobs it brings will more than make up for it.
Number 83.
What is the broadcast mainly about?
Number 84.
According to the speaker, which industry is expected to benefit?
Number 85.
Why does the speaker say?
But the jobs it brings will more than make up for it.
Questions 86 through 88 refer to the following broadcast.
Thanks so much for having me on the show, Gavin.
I'm here to tell your listeners about the Riverbend charity run,
which is happening next month.
I've spent the past year coordinating permits,
mapping out routes and lining up volunteers
because I wanted to give something back to our community
after helping with neighborhood fundraisers for years.
The proceeds will benefit the Maple Street Animal Shelter,
which cares for hundreds of animals every year.
On race day, runners can choose either a 5 kilometer or a 10 kilometer route,
and there will be food and live music afterward.
Registration opens this Friday on our website, so please sign up early.
Now, unlike some fundraisers where a portion of donations
covers operating expenses, local sponsors have generously underwritten
all our permits and supplies.
So I want everyone to know,
every single dollar we raise goes straight to the shelter.
Come out and join us.
Number 86.
Who most likely is the speaker?
Number 87.
What is the purpose of the event?
Number 88.
What does the speaker imply when he says,
every single dollar we raise goes straight to the shelter?
Questions 89 through 91 refer to the following excerpt from a meeting.
Good morning, everyone.
I've got some great news to share.
We've just landed the biggest order in our shop's history,
a full product catalog for a national retail chain.
Because the client needs every copy printed, packed,
and delivered to stores by the end of the month,
our turnaround this time is going to be very tight.
So before your shift starts today,
I need each of you to check your machines carefully
and make sure they're running properly.
This afternoon, I'll post the updated production schedule on the board
near the entrance, so please look it over before you head home.
Number 89.
What update does the speaker give?
Number 90.
What should the listeners do before their shifts begin?
Number 91.
What action will the speaker take later?
Questions 92 through 94 refer to the following excerpt from a meeting.
Going into the next quarter,
I'd like us to put more of our floor staff behind hands-on product demonstrations.
When people can actually try out a smart speaker
or set up a home security camera themselves,
they're far more likely to buy it.
All we need is for each of you to feel comfortable walking a shopper through the setup,
and I'm confident our sales figures will climb.
I know some of you are wondering about the cost,
but notice that our display table by the front entrance
has been almost empty since the holidays.
Over the next few weeks,
I'll also pair newer team members with someone more experienced.
Before we head back out,
Derek has put together a short training clip
showing exactly how a demonstration should go,
and I want everyone to see it with me.
Right after that, we'll go over next week's floor schedule.
Number 92.
Where does the speaker most likely work?
Number 93.
Why does the speaker say our display table by the front entrance
has been almost empty since the holidays?
Number 94.
What will the speaker most likely do next?
Questions 95 through 97 refer to the following telephone message and invoice.
Hello, this message is for Daniel in billing.
This is Marcus Vail at Hailwood Consulting,
calling about invoice 4817 from Brookmere office supplies,
which arrived this morning.
Since I work in our finance office,
I am reviewing the invoice against our purchase notes this afternoon.
At first, I suspected the storage cabinet's total,
but that line checks out on our records.
The real problem is the seating line.
We actually ordered fewer of those than the invoice shows for that row.
The meeting tables and desk lamps also look fine,
so only that one should be revised.
Could you please send me a corrected invoice with the proper amount?
Once I receive the revised copy, I'll send the full payment tomorrow morning.
Number 95.
In which department does the speaker work?
Number 96.
Look at the graphic.
Which quantity needs to be changed?
Number 97.
What does the speaker say he will do tomorrow?
Questions 98 through 100 refer to the following telephone message and price list.
Hi, Ms. Foster. This is Wendy from the events team.
I'm organizing the staff appreciation lunch for our department next month,
and I've been comparing the options from MedoFork catering.
I'm looking at their package list right now.
The group agreed that we should choose a package priced at $18 per person,
so that points me to just one package.
I know one of the others includes more dishes,
but I really don't think we need that much food for a lunch.
Since you're collecting the lunch replies from each team,
you probably have the latest count.
Anyway, before I place the order, could you confirm the final head count for me?
I'd need that number by Thursday at the latest.
Give me a call back when you get a chance.
Thanks, Ms. Foster.
Number 98.
Look at the graphic.
Which catering package is Wendy planning to order?
Number 99.
In the message, why does Wendy think Ms. Foster has the latest count?
Number 100.
After Ms. Foster provides the count, what is Wendy planning to do?
